newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian riots trials to start next week.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian riots trials to start next week.

text.p: The trial of 64 people charged with violent crimes and disobeying authorities during the riots in Jakarta on July 27 will begin next week, a court official said on Friday.
Budiman, a clerk in the criminal section of the Central Jakarta State Court, told Reuters the trials would begin on October 9.
"There are 64 people being tried in five trials on the same day under five panels of judges," he said.
They are being charged with using violence against people or property as well as disobeying orders from authorities to disperse, he said.

The Media Indonesia daily reported on Friday that another 60 people detained after the rioting would be tried in five other cases at a later date. All the suspects accused of criminal offences are being held in three Jakarta jails.

Police have said they detained 124 people after the riots in which the official National Commission on Human Rights said at least five people died, 149 were injured and 74 were reported missing. It was the worst violence in the city in 20 years.
The commission, which reported the figures of dead, injured and missing in its preliminary findings on August 31, is expected to release its final report on the riots sometime this month.
The commission revised down the number of people missing in the wake of the riots to 30 from 74, the Jakarta Post newspaper reported on Thursday.
Neither the government nor the military had acknowledged any missing people from the event.
The riots began after police raided the Jakarta office of the minority Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) on July 27 after it had been occupied by supporters of party leader Megawati Sukarnoputri.
Megawati, the daughter of late founding president Sukarno, had been ousted from the party leadership by rivals at a government-supported congress in June.

More than 100 vehicles, including a number of public buses, were burnt by rioters as they roamed over an area of more than three kms (1.9 miles) in central Jakarta after a large crowd of thousands of people around the headquarters was dispersed by police and troops.
A number of government buildings, banks and car showrooms were looted and burned by rioters over a 12-hour period.
A further 13 suspects, mostly members of the small left-wing People's Democratic Party (PRD), have been accused of subversion, which carries the death penalty in Indonesia.
The government has said the PRD, which it claims uses communist methods, was behind the riots.
Independent labour leader Muchtar Pakpahan was also arrested in the wake of the riots and charged with subversion.
Attorney-General Singgih, whose department is holding all those accused of subversion, has said those charged with subversion will go to trial in November.
